text:
**Short answer: about 300 W of solar recharges a 1,000 Wh station in one good day. A 200 W panel does it in about a day and a half.**

**The formula**

Panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charging losses, since panels rarely deliver their rated watts.

| Conditions | Panel watts for a full recharge in one day |
|---|---|
| Summer, ~5 peak sun hours | ~270-300 W |
| Average US day, ~4-4.5 hours | ~320-340 W |
| ~3 hours (shoulder season) | ~450 W |
| Northern winter, ~2 hours | ~735 W |

Sources: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) and [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/).

**If you'd rather take more than a day**
- A 200 W panel gives roughly 630 Wh on an average day (200 × 4.5 × 0.7), so about 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A quick rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, which gives about 200 W for a day and a half of decent sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A 100 W panel would take around 3 days.

**Check before you buy**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many watts it accepts. Panels beyond that add nothing. Mid-range 1,000-1,500 Wh units typically allow 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage window:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's accepted range. Going over can damage the charge controller. Wiring panels in series adds voltage, so check combined Voc.
- **Connector:** Panels usually have MC4 connectors, while stations often use XT60 or DC barrel ports, so you may need an adapter.
- **Using power while charging:** Net charging is solar input minus your load, so recharging takes longer if you're running devices.

**A panel option**

If your station accepts 400 W and a 12-60 V input, the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) fits. It has a 45.3 V Voc, MC4 output with XT60 and DC adapters included, and weighs 18.5 kg. It's listed at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (expires 2026-12-30). That link is an affiliate link, so the seller pays a commission at no cost to you. At about 1,260 Wh/day in average sun, it would recharge a 1,000 Wh station in under a day ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)). If your station's input is capped at 200 W, a 400 W panel is overkill, though it does help in weak light.
